chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you intend to wash the deceased, place a cloth between you and him to cover his private part from you, whether it is a shirt or something else. Then begin with his hands and his head, washing them three times with lotus leaves, then the rest of his body, and begin with his right side.

When you intend to wash his private part, take a clean rag and wrap it around your left hand, then insert your hand from beneath the cloth that is on the deceased's private part, and wash it without seeing his nakedness.

When you finish washing him with lotus leaves, wash him again with water and camphor, and something of his perfume. Then wash him with pure water with another washing, until when you have finished the three (washings), place him in a cloth, then dry him.
ai.seo_question: What is the step-by-step procedure for washing a deceased person in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the foundational methodology for *ghusl al-mayyit*, emphasizing the preservation of modesty (*awrah*) through the 'no direct sight' technique during the washing of the private parts. It prescribes a structured purification sequence using sidr (lotus leaves), camphor, and musk, reflecting the Shia emphasis on both physical cleanliness and spiritual dignity in preparing the deceased for burial.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When you want to wash the deceased, so make a cloth to be between you and him to veil his private part from you, whether it is a shirt or something else. Then begin with his palm and his head (washing it) three times with the lotus (leaves), then the rest of his body, and beginning with the right hand side.

So when you intend to wash his private part, then take a clean rag and wrap it around your right hand, then enter your hand from beneath the cloth which is upon the private part of the deceased, and wash it from without seeing his nakedness.

So when you are free from washing him with the lotus (leaves), then wash him again with water and camphor, and something from his embalming. Then wash him with pure water with another washing until when you are free from the three (washings), then make him to be in a cloth, then enshroud him’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

When you decide to give Ghusl (bath) to a dead body, you must keep a piece of cloth between yourself and the private parts of the dead body, like a shirt or similar. You should begin to wash the palms (hands) and the head of the dead body three times with water mixed with Sidr (berry leaves), then the rest of the body, first the right side.

When you decide to wash the private parts, you must take a clean piece of fabric, wrap your left hand with it, then enter your hand under the piece of cloth with which it is covered, then wash the private parts of the dead body without seeing them.

When you complete Ghusl (bath) with water mixed with Sidr (berry leaves), wash it a second time with water mixed with camphor and something with which Hunut is done; and thereafter wash the dead body with pure water. After completing all three Ghusl (baths) place the dead body on a piece of fabric and dry it up.’” (Ahadith 2-3 are best explained in the form of fatwa.)
